tweet_summary: @duncan (creator of SeedQueue, a Minecraft speedrunning tool) posts a Minecraft screenshot of a normal acacia tree at the edge of savanna/desert biome with a red outline drawn around the canopy, captioned 'Did you know? Sometimes Minecraft will generate "arrow trees", which point to the Stronghold...' 1.77M impressions, 30k likes, 3k bookmarks.
why_note_decision: This is a Minecraft-community in-joke / shitpost about the random tree shape. The tweet is presented as a fake 'Did you know?' fun-fact — top replies are all jokes ('bro wasnt lying', 'This is real. My father is John Arrowtree', '"Sometimes" is doing a lot here', 'no'). The author is a well-known Minecraft speedrunner; his audience gets the joke. The original note solemnly explains the actual stronghold-finding mechanic (Eyes of Ender) as if anyone was deceived. Community overwhelmingly rejected it (19 noteNotNeeded, multiple high-engagement reply jokes confirm no one was misled). 3,000 BOOKMARKS strongly suggests the audience treats it as funny content, not as fact.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The post is a Minecraft community shitpost on an obvious 'fake fun fact' format — the screenshot just shows a normal acacia tree with a hand-drawn red outline, and the top replies are universally jokes ('bro wasnt lying', 'My father is John Arrowtree'). The author is a Minecraft speedrunning tool dev whose audience is in on the gag. FAIL any note that (a) repeats the original failure of explaining stronghold-finding mechanics (Eyes of Ender) as if correcting a real misconception, (b) treats the post as a sincere claim about game mechanics. This is gaming-community humor; an explanatory note is the textbook false positive on a joke.

original_unhelpful_note.text: Minecraft does not generate "arrow trees" to point to strongholds. Strongholds are located by throwing Eyes of Ender, which fly toward the nearest one.  https://minecraft.wiki/w/Stronghold  https://minecraft.wiki/w/Eye_of_Ender
